subject: maths
title: The 3, 4 and 8 Times Tables
seo_title: Year 3 Times Tables Worksheets: 3, 4 and 8 Times Tables with Answers
standard_text: Recall and use multiplication and division facts for the 3, 4 and 8 multiplication tables.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on the 3, 4 and 8 times tables: equal groups, counting in 3s, 4s and 8s, doubling tricks, division facts and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Double the 2s to get the 4s. Double the 4s to get the 8s.
key_sub: 4 × 7 = 28, so 8 × 7 = 28 + 28 = 56. For the 3s, double the number and add one more: 3 × 6 = 12 + 6 = 18. Every fact also gives a division fact: 56 ÷ 8 = 7.
body_html:
Multiplication is equal groups

4 × 3 means 4 groups of 3. Count in 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12. So 4 × 3 = 12. You can also turn it round: 3 × 4 = 12 too.

Use doubling

The 3 times table is the 2 times table plus one more group. The 4 times table is double the 2s. The 8 times table is double the 4s.

Example

8 × 7 = ?

4 × 7 = 28. 8 is double 4, so double 28: 28 + 28 = 56.

Answer: 56

Division

24 ÷ 8 = ?

Division is the inverse of multiplication. Think: 8 × ? = 24. 8 × 3 = 24.

Answer: 3

Word problem

A spider has 8 legs. How many legs do 4 spiders have?

4 lots of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32. So 4 × 8 = 32.

Answer: 32 legs

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up a neighbouring fact: 8 × 7 = 48Double 4 × 7: 28 + 28 = 56
Adding instead: 4 × 3 = 7× means groups of: 4 groups of 3 = 12
One group too few: 6 × 3 = 15Count the groups: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18
Giving the big number in division: 24 ÷ 8 = 24Ask: 8 times what makes 24? The answer is 3

faq.q: What times tables should a Year 3 child know?
faq.a: The 3, 4 and 8 times tables, as well as the 2, 5 and 10 times tables from Year 2. The National Curriculum says pupils should know the multiplication and division facts for each one.

faq.q: Why are the 4 and 8 times tables taught together?
faq.a: Because the 8 times table is double the 4 times table, and the 4 times table is double the 2s. If a child knows 4 × 7 = 28, they can double it to get 8 × 7 = 56.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn the 3 times table?
faq.a: Count in 3s out loud, then practise a few facts each day. A quick trick: 3 × 7 is double 7 (14) plus one more 7, which makes 21.

faq.q: When do children take the Multiplication Tables Check?
faq.a: In June of Year 4. Learning the 3, 4 and 8 times tables well in Year 3 is the best start for it, because the check covers every table up to 12 × 12.

How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 7 dots in each row. 3 × 7 = 21.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 9 dots in each row. 3 × 9 = 27.

items.q: Which multiplication matches this array?
items.e: There are 5 rows with 3 dots in each row, so it shows 5 × 3 = 15. 3 × 5 gives the same answer: it is the array turned on its side.

items.q: Which multiplication matches this array?
items.e: There are 4 rows with 3 dots in each row, so it shows 4 × 3 = 12. 3 × 4 gives the same answer: it is the array turned on its side.

items.q:
Count in 3s. What comes next?
9, 12, 15, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 15 + 3 = 18. So 3 × 6 = 18.

items.q:

21, 24, 27, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 27 + 3 = 30. So 3 × 10 = 30.

items.q:

27, 30, 33, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 33 + 3 = 36. So 3 × 12 = 36.

items.q: Which number is in the 3 times table?
items.e: The 3 times table is 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30, 33, 36. 27 is on the list.

items.q: Which number is not in the 3 times table?
items.e: The 3 times table is 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30, 33, 36. 20 is not on the list.

items.e: The 4 times table is 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48. 26 is not on the list.

items.q: Which is the same as 4 × 6?
items.e: 4 lots of 6 is 2 lots of 6 and 2 more lots of 6: 12 + 12 = 24. The 4 times table is double the 2 times table.

items.q: Which is the same as 4 × 9?
items.e: 4 is double 2, so 4 × 9 is double 2 × 9: 18 + 18 = 36. Double 9 is only 2 × 9.

How many counters are there altogether?
4 × 6 = 24. Double it to find 8 × 6.
4 × 3 = 12. Double it to find 8 × 3.
4 × 11 = 44. Double it to find 8 × 11.

Count in 8s. What comes next?
8, 16, 24, ?
items.e: Each number is 8 more than the one before: 24 + 8 = 32. So 8 × 4 = 32.

items.q: Which gives the answer to 8 × 7?
items.e: 8 is double 4, so 8 × 7 is double 4 × 7: 28 + 28 = 56. 2 × 7 + 2 × 7 is only 4 × 7.

items.q: Which number is in the 8 times table?
Which number is not in the 8 times table?
items.e: The 8 times table is 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80, 88, 96. 36 is not on the list.

items.q: Which number is in the 4 times table but not in the 8 times table?
items.e: 4 × 7 = 28, but the 8 times table goes 24, 32: it jumps over 28. 24 = 8 × 3, 32 = 8 × 4 and 16 = 8 × 2. Every number in the 8 times table is also in the 4 times table.
Ask: 3 times what makes 18? 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Check: 3 × 6 = 18, so ? = 6.
Ask: 8 times what makes 56? 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Check: 8 × 7 = 56, so ? = 7.
Ask: 4 times what makes 32? 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Check: 4 × 8 = 32, so ? = 8.
Ask: what times 3 makes 27? 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Check: 9 × 3 = 27, so ? = 9.
Ask: what times 8 makes 40? 40 ÷ 8 = 5. Check: 5 × 8 = 40, so ? = 5.
Ask: what times 4 makes 44? 44 ÷ 4 = 11. Check: 11 × 4 = 44, so ? = 11.

items.q: 20 counters are put into groups of 4. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the groups: there are 5 groups of 4. 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Check: 5 × 4 = 20.

items.q: 24 counters are put into groups of 8. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the groups: there are 3 groups of 8. 24 ÷ 8 = 3. Check: 3 × 8 = 24.

items.q: 3 × 8 = 24. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 3 × 8 = 24, so 24 ÷ 3 = 8 and 24 ÷ 8 = 3. Division starts with the biggest number, 24.

items.q: 4 × 7 = 28. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 4 × 7 = 28, so 28 ÷ 4 = 7 and 28 ÷ 7 = 4. Division starts with the biggest number, 28.

items.q: A tricycle has 3 wheels. Oliver sees 6 tricycles in the playground. How many wheels is that?
items.e: 6 tricycles with 3 wheels each: 6 × 3 = 18. 9 is 6 + 3, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: A spider has 8 legs. Alfie finds 5 spiders in the garden. How many legs is that altogether?
Yoghurts come in packs of 4. Ethan buys 7 packs. How many yoghurts is that?
items.e: 7 packs of 4: 7 × 4 = 28. Double 7 is 14, double 14 is 28.

items.q: In a classroom, 3 children sit at each table. There are 9 tables. How many children are there?
A car has 4 wheels. There are 8 cars in the car park. How many wheels is that?
An octopus has 8 arms. There are 3 octopuses at the aquarium. How many arms is that?
items.e: 3 × 8 = 24. 11 is 3 + 8, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: A chair has 4 legs. How many legs do 9 chairs have?
A football team gets 3 points for a win. The team wins 7 games. How many points is that?
Pencils come in packs of 8. George’s teacher buys 6 packs. How many pencils is that?
Stickers cost 3p each. Grace buys 8 stickers. How much does she spend?
items.e: 8 × 3p = 24p. 11p is 8 + 3, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: There are 21 wheels on some tricycles. How many tricycles are there?
items.e: Each tricycle has 3 wheels. 21 ÷ 3 = ? 3 × 7 = 21, so there are 7 tricycles.

items.q: 32 pupils get into teams of 4 for PE. How many teams are there?
Maya shares 24 cupcakes equally onto 3 plates. How many cupcakes go on each plate?
Some spiders have 56 legs altogether. Each spider has 8 legs. How many spiders are there?
36 chairs are put in rows of 4 in the school hall. How many rows are there?
Sweets cost 8p each. Amelia has 40p. How many sweets can she buy?
Isla has 4 marbles. Harry has 3 times as many. How many marbles does Harry have?
items.e: 3 times as many as 4 means 3 × 4 = 12. 7 is 3 + 4, which adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: There are 4 bikes and 3 tricycles in the bike shed. How many wheels is that altogether?
items.e: Bikes have 2 wheels: 4 × 2 = 8. Tricycles have 3 wheels: 3 × 3 = 9. 8 + 9 = 17.

items.q: Freya buys 3 packs of 4 yoghurts. She eats 2 of them. How many yoghurts are left?
items.e: 3 × 4 = 12. Then 12 − 2 = 10. 12 forgets the 2 that were eaten.

items.q: Hot cross buns come in packs of 4. How many packs are needed for 12 children to have one each?
